subject: pack/unpack "U" works in UTF-8 bytes, not codepoints (uni/sprintf.t t21-23)
description:
DECIDED s317 (fable-answers-s316v.md §6j): implement the FULL mode model — mode state threaded through _pack_tmpl/_unpack_tmpl, default CHARACTER mode (`U` = codepoint directly; SBCL native strings need no encoding step), `U0` enters / `C0` leaves byte mode, mid-template; drop the prefix-only pre-encode. Check `W` vs `C` in the same pass. Rule 12 safety valve: any template feature you choose not to implement DIES loudly naming the template — never a silent wrong value. Dev harness: cl/pack-impl.pl runs under REAL perl — diff it against native pack/unpack directly (perfect oracle, no SBCL in the loop) before transpiling. Post-R1 (W2.5); tools/rebuild-pack in the SAME commit.

uni/sprintf.t is perl 52/0 vs PCL 49/3; t21/t22/t23 all reduce to the `U` template letter.

  my $s = "\x{1234}";        # length 1, ord 4660 — PCL agrees so far
  unpack("U*", $s)        perl 4660   PCL 4
  ord(pack("U",0x1234))   perl 4660   PCL 225   (0xE1 = first UTF-8 byte of U+1234)

ROOT IS A MODE MODEL, NOT AN ENCODING SLIP. perl's pack has two modes:
  - CHARACTER mode (the DEFAULT): `U` packs/unpacks the codepoint directly.
  - BYTE mode, entered by `U0` (and left by `C0`): `U` encodes/decodes UTF-8 bytes. The switches are MID-TEMPLATE, not just a prefix.

cl/pack-impl.pl has this inverted:
  - the `U` letter ALWAYS routes through _pack_utf8_char (line 397) / _unpack_utf8_char (762), i.e. always BYTE-mode behaviour;
  - `U0` is handled separately at ~1161 as a template PREFIX only (`$tmpl =~ s/^U0//`), pre-encoding the whole input — so `U0` currently means "transform twice", not "switch mode".

SCOPE / RISK: pack is the most heavily tested area in the corpus (blessed 5635 pass / 90 fail). cl/pcl-pack.lisp is a CHECKED-IN TRANSPILED ARTIFACT: `tools/rebuild-pack` in the SAME commit, then `perl sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 1 --timeout 380 perl-tests/pack.t` + tools/sweep-diff.pl (expect 0 new), then the full gate+sweep.

Probes: scratchpad w0/sp1.pl, sp2.pl.
